1 · The Scout finds what is worth a look. The whole screened universe graded twice, independently: the Owner's Scorecard asks how good the business is (Buffett); the Inversion Layer asks how it would lose your money (Munger). The two verdicts are never merged — a name can be Exceptional and Fragile at once, and that tension is the information. Click any row for the full drill-down.

2 · The Thesis Desk turns the best 1% into written, testable theses. Every candidate gets a work order; an agent (Claude Code / OpenClaw) researches it and writes a draft — business model, moat evidence, owner earnings, bear case, and at least three pre-committed invalidation triggers. Python re-checks every rule mechanically and refuses what it cannot verify. The draft then waits for the owner at the Gate: conviction and the buy decision are never generated (FR9).

The three-beat seam

no LLM API client anywhere — the agent harness IS the runtime
1

brief

python thesis.py batch writes a work order per candidate: the research packet (both judgements, unmerged), the framework, the trigger rules, the schema.

2

the agent researches

Web research with its own tools, then writes report.md, summary.md, thesis.json. Trusted for research and prose — never for the contract.

3

record

python thesis.py record re-checks every rule mechanically — including which model did the work (best-available only, read from the harness, not asked of the agent) — and exits non-zero if it refuses.

3 · The Monitor checks every committed thesis against its own triggers, weekly. Never open-ended news scanning: the thesis drives the monitoring. Metric triggers are pure arithmetic on fresh filings (with the tier-2 enrichment cache, so a leverage trigger stays checkable); judgement questions go to the agent and an unanswered one is reported UNCHECKED, loudly. A tripped break trigger means the standing advice is to sell, ignoring cost basis (FR7) — and nothing here ever executes a trade (FR11). “No action needed” is the celebrated outcome (FR4).

The weekly loop

three commands, one report
python monitor.py brief --theses-dir theses # 1 · the open judgement questions # the agent answers them into theses/monitor-<date>/verdicts.json python monitor.py run --sec-data <dir> --prices <dir> \ --enrich-cache enrich_cache \ --verdicts theses/monitor-<date>/verdicts.json # 2 · evaluate everything → reports/monitor-<date>.md

Confidence is mechanical: only high (documented public fact) lets a break trigger actually break — anything less demotes to review, because an inference must never fire a sell rule. A narrative trigger can only summon the owner to the desk.
